subject: Pilot guarantee & retainer: sculpting a staged SLA for Vectra Health
messages:

To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@vectrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot guarantee & retainer: initial ask

Irene —

Thanks for the demo last week. Vectra is interested in running a 3-month inference pilot (production traffic slice) and we need a clear commitment on availability and escalation. Two quick asks to start the pricing conversation:  

1) Can Redwood commit to a measurable uptime guarantee for the pilot (we're targeting 99.9% for the slice)?
2) We need an on-call escalation path for Sev1s — 24/7 with named escalation contacts.

This will be a purchase from procurement if we can land a straightforward retainer + consumption offer with a small pilot discount. Megan (CC) will loop in procurement if we move forward. Can you send a short proposal and any standard SLA language you can share?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Bennett
VP Platform Engineering, Vectra Health

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Sam Bennett <sam@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@vectrahealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot guarantee & retainer: initial ask

Sam —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Below is a concise pilot structure that balances predictability for Vectra and our ability to operate a short-term production slice. I've attached a priced spreadsheet and a draft SLA excerpt. High level:  

Pilot structure (3 months):
- Retainer: $18,000 / month (covers reserved slot, priority routing, basic cache warming)
- Consumption: billable at standard hosted rates for tokens/embeddings beyond retainer credit
- Pilot discount: 10% off list consumption for the pilot term

Availability / credits (pilot-specific heartbeat guarantee):
- Baseline guarantee: 99.5% for the pilot slice; objective is 99.9% but for short pilots we set 99.5% with a measured ramp clause
- Credits: pro-rated monthly credit calculated as (1 - availability) * monthly retainer (example and formula in attached SLA draft)

Escalation & response windows:
- Business-hours triage (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT): 60-minute initial response, Sev1 follow-up at 2 hours
- 24/7 named escalation: Available, but requires the Enhanced Escalation Retainer add-on (see pricing below)

Optional add-on — Enhanced Escalation Retainer:
- $6,000 / month: named oncall (phone handoff), committed 30-minute incident response window, weekly bridge facilitation, and prioritized bugfix queueing for pilot-impacting regressions

Discounting note: If Vectra converts to a 12-month committed plan at pilot close, we can apply an additional 12% back-of-book credit to the first 3 months' consumption.

Attachments: pilot_pricing_v3.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft-aug-2026.pdf

Next step: If this looks directionally right I can loop Karthik (pricing) and Laura (legal/SOW) to prepare a one-page SOW + DocuSign for signature.

—
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Irene —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few items from procurement/engineering that we'll need before we can sign:  

- Can you move the pilot baseline to 99.9% (or make 99.9% an objective with a two-tier credit that favors us if you miss)?
- The Enhanced Escalation Retainer is interesting; procurement wants to see the hourly breakdown and whether that fee converts into credits if we sign a longer-term commitment.
- We need SOC 2 evidence + the specific list of audit logs you provide for the pilot (particularly token-level access and data retention for embeddings).

Budget-wise: procurement is pushing for a lower retainer — $12k / month would be easier to approve as an initial pilot. If you can keep the consumption discount and show a clear conversion incentive, we may be able to sign quickly.

Can your legal team share a short SLA excerpt with the two-tier credit model?

Thanks,
Megan

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@vectrahealth.com>, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot guarantee & retainer: initial ask (pricing alternatives)

Megan / team —

Looping in a couple of alternative constructs that can hit Vectra's ask while protecting the pilot economics. Two short options:  

Option A — Lower retainer, staged availability:
- Retainer: $12,000 / month (matches procurement ask)
- Consumption: +12% surcharge vs standard list (to cover the smaller reserved slot)
- Availability: 99.9% target; credit banding: 99.9–99.0 = 25% of monthly retainer credit, <99.0 = 50% credit (formula in SLA draft)

Option B — Moderate retainer + Enhanced Escalation as built-in:
- Retainer: $15,000 / month
- Enhanced Escalation included (30-minute named oncall)
- Availability guarantee: 99.5% baseline with an automatic uplift trigger: if availability <99.9 for two consecutive weeks, we commit a corrective runbook and a one-time service credit equal to 40% of that month's retainer

SOC 2 + evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 report (redacted), plus a scoped log export for the pilot. We'll include explicit retention and redaction options in the SOW.

Legal/credit wording suggestion (snippet):
"If Provider fails to meet the availability thresholds set for the Pilot, Provider will issue a credit to Customer's account proportional to the measured unavailability for the affected month(s). Credits are applied to future invoices and do not constitute a waiver of other remedies."  

Happy to take a quick call to walk through Option A vs B. If procurement prefers the $12k retainer, Option A gets us live faster; Option B gives Vectra more rapid operational support out of the box.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Sam Bennett <sam@vectrahealth.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@vectrahealth.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot guarantee & retainer: initial ask — proposed closing path

Sam / Megan —

Thanks for the fast back-and-forth. Based on the feedback here's a pragmatic close path that should be easy for procurement and keeps the pilot focused on proving latency/accuracy and escalation workflows:  

Agreed pilot (3 months):
- Agreed monthly retainer: $12,000 / month (Option A)
- Consumption pricing: standard hosted rates with pilot 10% consumption discount (as originally proposed)
- Availability & credits: two-tier crediting 
  - >=99.9%: no credit
  - 99.0%–99.9%: 25% of monthly retainer credited pro-rata for impacted month
  - <99.0%: 50% of monthly retainer credited pro-rata for impacted month
- Enhanced Escalation: optional add-on at $6,000 / month (convertible to credit if Vectra signs a 12-month commitment within 60 days of pilot end; conversion equals 75% of paid add-on fees applied to first invoice post-conversion)
- SOC 2: we will share our redacted SOC 2 report and a scoped log export for pilot testing; we will include explicit redaction controls in the SOW

Next steps: I will have Laura produce a one-page SOW + short SLA excerpt and a DocuSign envelope by EOD Monday. If Vectra signs, we will kick off onboarding and schedule the named oncall handoff (if Enhanced Escalation is selected).

If this is acceptable Sam/Megan, please reply with an approval line and any mandatory PO terms procurement requires.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot scheduled.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
